hypothesis: A deterministic, execution-aware catalog document representation will improve retrieval of ordinary versus specialised ball-valve variants while preserving selection semantics.
why_now: The repository’s current catalog documents contain raw names and properties but no normalized execution descriptors. Current hard failures include specialised variants being returned for ordinary technical requests. This is the highest-value untested retrieval-side intervention and requires the first of the five allowed index rebuilds.
expected_effect: Dense and BM25 retrieval both gain bounded Russian descriptors for explicit underground, regulating/Regula, cryogenic, gas-specific, electric-ready, ordinary, full-passage, and standard-passage evidence; raw catalog text, query processing, RRF, reranking, and final selection remain unchanged.
expected_metric_gain: +3.3–6.7 percentage points hard-pass coverage, with no intended safety regression.
lesson_from_history: Cycles 1, 2, and 5 established that candidate gating and selection/prompt changes can regress safety or coverage. Cycles 3–4 showed deterministic retrieval changes can help, while Cycle 6 showed narrow query-only expansion alone is not reliably sufficient. No prior cycle has tested catalog-side structural enrichment or used an index rebuild.
candidate_hypotheses: Execution-aware catalog document enrichment with a bounded index rebuild (selected).
Flange-subtype schema expansion for weld-neck/butt-weld requirements.
A second reranker or post-rerank compatibility decision layer.
plan_summary: Created and strict-validated the complete OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/cycle-07-execution-aware-catalog-representation/: proposal, execution-aware-catalog-representation delta spec, design, and implementation-only focused tasks. No product code or evaluation artifacts were edited.
